_doc: McCready's Opera House (#1143): the building lab's step 2, the spec on its lot, written by tools/buildings/opera_house_spec.py (edit it, not this). NOT BUILT: the build waits for after the slice; keys marked NEW are parts the builder doesn't have (experiments/building_lab/opera_house/README.md). Sizes here, the look on the sheet (experiments/building_lab/opera_house/sheet).

identity.owner: Ezra McCready, who sold his share in the Argentine lode in 1880 and built the town something to be proud of (and a stage for his wife's sister)
identity.trade: an opera house: travelling companies, melodrama, a singer with the band, lectures, the magic lantern, the Fourth of July ball, the Miners' Union meetings
identity.means: the only brick building in Salt Creek but the bank: freighted-in brick, plate glass, iron, three hundred opera chairs from Chicago, scenery painted in Denver
identity.age_and_repair: 1 year: the brick new and sharp, the walk already worn at the doors; one lane window boarded where a drunk put a bottle through
clues: a stack of old show bills behind the box office
cigar ash ground into the foyer's carpet
a banjo case and a pair of dancing shoes left in a dressing room
chalk seat numbers on the backs of the chairs
a bucket of sand and a bucket of water by the footlights

lot._doc: valley.json town.north (NEW lot, added at the build, not before: a valley change can tip the card-game tests): past the undertaker's (x 106-128) a lane x 128.0-130.4 (8 ft: the hall's west exits), the lot x 130.4-149.0 by the town's 125 ft depth to Back Street; Main Street's and Back Street's x [-125, 130] grow to 150. The East Road still leaves from (130, 0) south-east, clear of the walk. The building's origin its EAST front corner (facing 180). The ground (ValleyTerrain.height, 2026-11-24): -0.44 (west) to -0.58 (east) at the front line, +0.18..+0.06 at 20 m back, +0.84..+0.38 at 30 m (Back Street's bank): a pad dug level at the walk's street edge (y -0.5) under the building and its yard, a bank left behind.

walk.why: A brick front needs no awning; three wide stone-edged steps across the three doorways for a crowd and ladies' skirts.

levels._doc: The hall's floor at the walk's top; the stage, the dressing block and the lower boxes 3 ft 6 in over it; the foyer and the balcony's back aisle 5 m over it (the lobby 16 ft high); the scene loft over the foyer; the hall's trusses on the plate 10 m over the floor, its plaster ceiling under them (32 ft); the stage house's gridiron 30 ft over the stage. NEW levels: stage, attic, dress_upper, dress_roof, front_roof (the builder knows cellar, ground and upper).

frame._doc: A load-bearing brick building, timber floors and roof. Brick walls by Kidder (public halls: 17 in to the upper floor, 13 in above; 13 in for the fire wall and the dressing block), lime mortar, on sandstone footings 4 ft down (below Colorado's frost). Joists by the Wood Handbook's working stresses (yellow pine, 1,200 lb/in2 bending; deflection L/360), 100 lb/ft2 where a crowd stands (Kidder's for theatres), 70 the dance floor, 40 the lofts and roofs (snow). `--sizing` prints each (the README's table). Dressed sizes, metres [width, depth].

stone_wall._doc: NEW use: the jail's stone walls laid as BRICK (`masonry` brick; BrickWall, the README's parts): members as lifts of nine courses (0.6 m, the jail's course) and 1.2 m long, so the walls are ~2,000 members, not 100,000 bricks; chips by the voxel carving, a charge drops lifts. Common bond (a header course every sixth), 8 x 4 x 2 1/4 in bricks, 3/8 in joints: the shader's. Dressed buff sandstone: the quoins, the base course, sills, keystones over the arches, the coping.

walls._doc: The front on Main Street: red brick in common bond on a buff sandstone base course (to the walk's top), dressed quoins at both corners, stone sills and keystones; 17 in to the foyer's floor, 13 in above (the set-off carries the foyer's joists). Three tiers (Sean, #1242): three arched doorways (pairs of glazed doors opening OUT, fanlights; cast-iron columns at the middle one: `front.iron_columns`) and an arched window either side; five tall arched foyer windows; five small arched attic windows (the scene loft). The galvanized-iron cornice on paired brackets, its frieze MCCREADY'S OPERA HOUSE in gilt, the pediment's roundel 1881.

balcony._doc: NEW (`Balcony` kind `horseshoe`, the README's parts): the deck in tiers stepped 0.3 m (each tier a floor of its own on raking carriages: 3x12 at 16 in from the rail beam up to pockets in the brick and the lobby's back wall), the rail beam 8x12 on nine cast-iron columns (6 in, 3/4 in metal), the corners' beam as 0.6 m chords (a ball or charge brings down a segment, not the sweep); the front a panelled gilt fascia on the rail's line with a velvet-padded rail 0.75 m over the front row. 100 lb/ft2. The columns stand on brick piers through the hall's floor. Clear under the rail: 3.45 m.

boxes._doc: NEW (`Balcony` kind `box`): four boxes, two a side, one over the other, between the side arms' ends and the proscenium wall: joists 3x10 in pockets in the side wall and the proscenium, the front on a cast-iron column at its outer corner. The lower boxes' floor at the stage's height (entered through the proscenium wall's passage doors, or four steps up from the hall's side aisle); the upper ones off the side arms' passages.

seats._doc: The parquet (Sean, 2026-11-24: about 300 in all): eight rows of 26 in one block, 32 in rows, 20 in folding opera chairs on cast-iron standards (A. H. Andrews & Co.'s), screwed down; the front four rows on runners (cleared for a ball); behind them standing room under the balcony. Side aisles along the walls under the balcony's side arms (its side columns in them); a column that stands in a row takes a seat's place (`out`: the period's 'obstructed by a post'). A kit prop by the prop lab (`opera_chair`, NEW).

stage._doc: The stage (saloon B's `stage` grown up, #902's form: legs, bearers, joists, boards, a skirt): 3 ft 6 in over the hall, the full width behind the proscenium and an apron 4 ft out of it with the footlights' trough; a trap 4 x 4 ft between two joists (the church's hatch rule); the gridiron 30 ft over the stage on beams in pockets (3x8 slats, open between); the drop curtain and three roll drops on battens hung from it by ropes made off at the pin rail (the Rope part) on the west fly gallery; wings of flats either side. NEW: the apron, the trough, the gridiron, the battens, the pin rail, the gallery.

steps._doc: down to the pit's east end (acts into the house)

drops.art: a painted lake under mountains in a painted gilt frame

fly_gallery._doc: a gallery along the west wall at the dressing block's upper floor, for the flymen, on brackets in the brick; its door to the upper dressing rooms

roof._doc: NEW (`HoweTruss`, the README's parts): over the hall, four Howe trusses on the pilasters at 12 ft, spanning 59 ft; over the stage house two more; the front block and the dressing block flat behind their parapets (floors of level front_roof and dress_roof). Purlins 4x10 at the panel points, rafters 2x8 at 24 in, 1 in boards, terne plate (tin), 3/12 to a ridge 2.1 m over the plate, under the hall's parapets' line seen from the street (the front block hides it). The hall's ceiling: 2x8 at 16 in hung from the bottom chords by iron straps, lath and plaster under them, a cove at the walls, a plaster rose round the chandelier's chain in the middle bay.

truss._doc: rods 1 5/8 in at the ends, 1 1/4 next, 1 in in the middle panels (wrought iron, nuts on cast angle blocks); the bottom chord two 6x12 bolted with keys (Haupt)

ceilings._doc: Plaster on lath (NEW: `PlasterWall`, the README's parts: cracks, falls in chunks off its lath, the paper tearing with it) in every room, the hall's under the trusses (the roof's `ceiling`), the lobby's and foyer's with a cornice and a rose.

inside_finish._doc: NEW finishes: walnut wainscot to 3 ft (the lobby, the foyer, the hall), wallpaper over plaster above (deep red and gold, three bands), plain plaster and whitewash backstage and in the dressing rooms; the brick bare in the stage house.

stairs._doc: the lobby's two stairs: straight flights of 26 risers (7.6 in on 10 in treads) against the bar's and the parlour's walls, rising from the vestibule's side to a landing at the lobby's back wall, its door straight into the balcony (the gallery's to the foyer); turned walnut newels at the foot, a red runner on brass rods; their open sides railed. The wells over them the flights' length.
